title: Isolate policy runtime and compact regional routing mapper
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce runtime contention and memory overhead in the Smart Router by extracting the policy evaluation runtime out of the hot request path and replacing the current region->shard mapping with a compact, read-optimized mapper.

Background: The current routing hot path performs policy evaluation, regional affinity resolution, and fallback selection under shared locks in the request loop. This causes tail-latency amplification under bursty traffic and makes it hard to introduce more advanced fallback heuristics. We've accumulated ad-hoc sharding maps and protobuf schemas that are heavy on allocations and require frequent GC under load.

This ticket implements three coordinated changes:
1) Policy runtime isolation: spin up a lightweight, lock-free policy evaluator service (in-process worker pool with immutable input) that materializes decision tokens for fast lookup in the hot path. The hot path will only read a compact token and not run full policy logic.
2) Compact regional mapper: replace the in-memory region->shard mapping with a contiguous, memory-packed structure (flat arrays + versioned pointer) enabling atomic swaps on updates so reads are lockless and consistent.
3) Dependency cleanup: bump protobuf/grpc client libs to the validated versions used by infra (minimize intermediate allocations), and remove a legacy routing shim that serializes decision context into heavyweight structs.

Acceptance criteria:
- p50/p95 latency in the router hot path reduced by at least 10% and 15% respectively in the canary environment for typical production traces.
- Fallback selection correctness matches current behavior for 99.9% of requests during rollout tests (explicit regression set to capture edge cases).
- No more global mutexes on routing decision path in the runtime binary (auditable via code search and CI tests).
- Migration path: feature-flagged rollout + staged canaries by region, with automatic rollback trigger if error rate > 0.2% or latency regression > 25% in any canary region.

Migration plan:
- Phase 1: implement isolated policy runtime and feature flag. Unit tests + integration harness. Canary deploy to us-west-2 with 1% traffic.
- Phase 2: deploy compact mapper and protobuf upgrades together behind the same flag. Expand canary to eu-west-1 and ap-south-1.
- Phase 3: monitor for 72 hours, run regression eval suite, then graduate and remove legacy shim after 2 weeks of stable metrics.

Risks & mitigations:
- Behavior drift in fallback ordering: maintain a regression prompt set and add a scoreboard for top-10 divergent queries.
- Upgrade-induced incompatibilities: pin protobuf schemas in a compatibility test and run cross-version integration tests in CI.
- Rollback complexity: keep single-line fallback to previous runtime token using version header in requests.
